# Вярно · vyarno.bg

> «Икономиката, честно» — the economy, honestly. A calculator that measures
> Bulgaria's official statistics against one household's own numbers: personal
> inflation, real wage, salary percentile, the tax wedge, rent, savings and the
> path to a home. Every figure comes from a named publisher and carries the
> period it describes and a link to the publisher's own table.

Written in English, which is the convention for this format and what an agent
parses; the service name and the attribution line below stay in Bulgarian.

## Pages

Every page is served at two addresses: the Bulgarian one below and the same
path under /en/. Each document is in one language and declares the other as its
hreflang alternate, so quote whichever you read and cite its own URL.

- https://vyarno.bg/ — the calculator. What a household's own basket, pay and
  housing costs did against the official series. The arithmetic runs in the
  reader's browser and nothing they type is sent anywhere.
- https://vyarno.bg/how/ — the country's figures, explained and dated:
  inflation by the 13 COICOP divisions, tax and social contributions, the pay
  distribution, mortgage rates, Sofia €/m² and unemployment. The pay
  distribution and the wages there are the country's; the €/m² is Sofia's,
  because имот.bg publish by city and no national level exists.
- https://vyarno.bg/market/ — the residential property market, from the
  institutions' own figures: how many dwellings households bought in the
  quarter, what was paid for them, Eurostat's own annual rate of change on the
  house price index, who owns and who owes, the census dwelling stock and the
  price-to-income ratio against its own long-run average. No input on the page.
  Every figure carries its publisher, the period it describes and a link; every
  figure that is our arithmetic states the arithmetic and links the queries
  that reproduce it. The page takes no position on the market — several of the
  figures on it point in different directions and all of them are shown.
- https://vyarno.bg/credit/ — what borrowing costs in Bulgaria: the rate on a
  new home loan, the same loans' APRC, what the book already being repaid
  averages, and how long the rate on new lending is fixed for — 99.6% of it
  carries a rate the bank may change within a year. Also how much of what is
  reported as new lending is an existing loan repriced, and the БНБ limits
  every mortgage is bound by. No input on the page, and no lender named on it:
  БНБ's registers are linked so a reader can check their own.
- https://vyarno.bg/legal/ — terms of use, privacy, the provider's identity
  under ЗЕТ чл. 4, and each upstream's own licence wording.
- https://vyarno.bg/support/ — who pays for the project. It is free for
  everyone, has no paid tier, and donations buy nothing.
- https://vyarno.bg/en/ — the calculator, in English
- https://vyarno.bg/en/how/ — the country's figures, in English
- https://vyarno.bg/en/market/ — the residential property market, in English
- https://vyarno.bg/en/credit/ — what borrowing costs, in English
- https://vyarno.bg/en/legal/ — terms, privacy and the sources, in English
- https://vyarno.bg/en/support/ — who pays for the project, in English

## The published figures

Thirteen JSON payloads, refreshed by a pipeline and committed to the repository.
Each carries `as_of`, the reference period, and `source_url` to the publisher's
own table.

- hicp_headline — Eurostat's all-items HICP rate for Bulgaria, and the index
- hicp_categories — the 13 divisions, their official weights and each rate
- payroll — the tax and social-contribution table, gross to net
- region_salary — the НСИ quarterly average wage in each of the 28 области
- sector_salary — the НСИ quarterly average wage by economic activity, 19 NACE
  Rev 2 sections and the all-activities total. An average, not a median: nobody
  publishes how pay is spread within a Bulgarian sector, so there is no rank
  here to read. The all-activities total is the level the pay distribution is
  re-levelled onto
- salary_dist — the pay distribution, Eurostat SES shape re-levelled onto that
  national average. It is the country's at every oblast: no publisher measures
  how pay is spread inside one
- city_price — €/m² across the districts of each covered city, and how far back
  имот.bg's coverage of that city supports a comparison. `city_pages` lists
  every city имот.bg serve a page for, so a city a refresh has not reached is
  never reported as one they do not publish
- credit — what a Bulgarian household pays for money that is not a home loan:
  the rate and APRC on consumer credit, the rate on overdrafts and revolving
  lines, and the rate on a credit-card balance carried past the interest-free
  period (about 21%). Plus what a deposit pays, because a borrowing rate is
  only high or low against something. ECB MIR, monthly. Card and overdraft
  carry no volume and no APRC — BG reports neither, so how much such debt is
  carried is not published by anyone.
- house_market — Eurostat's quarterly property series: dwellings sold split
  new and existing, what was paid for them in euro, the house price index and
  Eurostat's own annual rate of change. `avg_deal_eur` is OURS — value divided
  by count, per quarter and purchase type — disclosed as a derivation under
  Eurostat's reuse conditions, with `derived_from_api_urls` carrying the two
  queries that reproduce it. These are dwellings bought by households at the
  price paid; the land register counts every sale deed and runs more than twice
  as high for the same quarter
- house_market_structure — tenure (who owns, who owns with a loan, who rents at
  a market price), the census dwelling stock and how much of it stood
  unoccupied, the price-to-income ratio against its own long-run average, and
  the housing-cost overburden rate. Every figure a published cell; the
  unoccupied share is derived in the browser from the two counts here
- nsi_housing — НСИ's own housing statistics: the national house price index
  change on the same quarter a year earlier, the same figure for the six cities
  over 120,000 people, and the change in the NUMBER of sales for those cities.
  Every value is a cell НСИ published — their licence forbids distributing
  производни и сборни произведения, so there is no gap, ratio, rank or level in
  this file. No level exists to carry: every НСИ city series is an index or a
  percentage and their лв./кв.м survey ran to 2014-Q2 and was discontinued, so
  **no transaction price per square metre is published for any Bulgarian city by
  anyone**. The national change here is the same statistic Eurostat disseminate
  in house_market.json, by a second route, and the pipeline gates them against
  each other
- mortgage — home-loan rates and the БНБ borrowing caps
- unemployment — the monthly seasonally adjusted rate

## Getting the data by machine

Take it from the repository: https://github.com/vyarno-bg/vyarno — it is
versioned, it carries the schema and the refresh history, and it costs a small
server nothing. Reading the JSON off this site is not the route: robots.txt
disallows the published-data directory for every crawler group, and the terms
of use name the repository instead.

## Licence and attribution

Данни от Евростат / ЕЦБ / НСИ / БНБ / имот.bg

The CODE is Apache-2.0. The FIGURES are not ours to license: they belong to
five publishers — Eurostat, the European Central Bank, НСИ (the Bulgarian
National Statistical Institute), БНБ (the Bulgarian National Bank) and imot.bg
— each under its own terms, and НСИ's forbid redistributing derived and
composite works. Cite the publisher named beside a figure, not this site, and
read https://vyarno.bg/legal/#sources for each one's wording.

If you quote a number from here, quote its period with it. A rate without the
month it describes is the thing this project exists to replace.
